skills.name: Mining
skills.summary: extracts ore, gems and minerals
tiers: You are no star-gazer, but you might dig up a few chunks of iron ore if you are very lucky. Quicksilver or corundum are clearly beyond you.
You have learned to handle a pick—not master it, but well enough. You are decent at mining iron, the most common metal.
You have made your mark in the mining trade. You can now mine corundum and quicksilver, and you know the first rule of orichalcum: avoid the Orcs.
You can tell moonstone from other minerals. Rare metals like gold and silver require knowledge, and you have it.
Your beard has grown fuller and your collar higher. Any stone in a backwater gully speaks to you; you know how to wrest something valuable from it—malachite, perhaps even ebony.

skills.name: Fishing
skills.summary: catches fish
tiers: You know there is such a thing as a rod and that you can put bait on the hook. You even know you must cast and watch the float—but does that guarantee a catch? Hardly.
You have learned the basics of fishing and now know that river fish bite best on bee or lunar moth wing.
Thanks to long trips and hours at the line, you have found that lake fish love dragonfly most, and dungeon fish will strike at any bait.
You are an experienced fisher. You know saltwater fish bite well on blue butterfly and monarch, and that predatory fish in any water go for fighting fish.
You fish like a master. Many think you are just lucky, but you know the right spot, the right bait, and a steady hand matter far more.

skills.name: Saltmaking
skills.summary: harvests sea salt deposits and grinds salt at grain mills
tiers: You know salt comes from the coast, but a pickaxe and a grain mill still feel like guesswork.
You can chip sea salt rock from coastal deposits and grind it into salt piles at a mill.
Long hours on the shore teach you where Fire Salts sometimes cling to the rock.
Your eye for frost-kissed veins lets you keep Frost Salts when fortune favors you.
Masters of the salt trade pull Void Salts from the same deposits others leave barren—and waste nothing at the mill.

skills.name: Hunting
skills.summary: harvests pelts and meat from wild animals
tiers: Hunting is no simple trade, especially for a beginner. Catching wily rabbits or mudcrabs takes more knowledge than you have.
You have learned the basics of the hunt, but lack practice—you often ruin pelts and ingredients when butchering in the field.
You have hunted long enough to take the choicest ingredients, but you are still careless with skinning away from a proper table.
You are an experienced hunter; your quarry grows larger and your butchering is good enough to stay far from cities.
You know where to find rare beasts and how to hunt them. You do not miss when skinning or harvesting valuable parts.

skills.name: Herbalism
skills.summary: gathers herbs, mushrooms and berries
tiers: Your plant lore may begin and end with grandmother's tales of edible berries. Your last stomach upset has made you doubt her expertise.
"The Barbarian's Primer" has helped you recognise some plants; you now know how to pick blue mountain flower without drawing minotaurs.
You always liked mushrooms but not gathering them. Time to change. You know a lot about fungi and can easily tell which one poisoned you yesterday.
Your wanderings through woods, fields and caves have paid off. You know herbs, berries and mushrooms well, and have secret spots—any herbalist's pride.
You have reached the peak of herbalism. You can tell one plant from another at a glance. Your clothes smell of flowers, no worse than Telvanni bug musk.

skills.name: Woodcutting
skills.summary: chops firewood and burns charcoal at the kiln
tiers: Novice: chop firewood and burn charcoal dust at the kiln.
Apprentice: lump charcoal from denser burns.
Adept: proper charcoal for forges and hearths.
Expert: charcoal briquettes for hotter, cleaner fires.
Master: charcoal coke—the peak of the charcoal burner's craft.

skills.name: Beekeeping
skills.summary: catch wild bees, tend hives, and gather honeycomb (tiered by hive type)
tiers: Novice: tend ordinary and vacant hives and catch wild bees. Honeycomb and bees are your teachers.
Apprentice: work larger farm apiaries (Mereth and similar). Yields improve with practice.
Adept: work large estate hives such as Goldenglow. You handle aggressive swarms without panic.
Expert: your apiaries thrive; wax and comb come easily, and wild bees rarely escape you.
Master: breeding, feeding, and turning comb into wax and foundation are second nature.

skills.name: Farming
skills.summary: grows and harvests crops, keeps chickens and cattle
tiers: You know how to dig potatoes. Don't you?
A farmer has many tasks: tend crops, milk cows, feed chickens, collect eggs, haul manure, fill the cellar for winter. You can do it all, but only barely.
Your cheese and butter output grows; harvests and milk yields rise, and the hens lay like mad. An idyll built on your labour.
You have learned many tricks and methods. Maximising yield is your creed—and never let tramps past the fence; they will trample more than they steal.
Your parents envy your farming success; you are a master without doubt. If not yours, someone's parents envy you. Everyone does.

skills.name: Lockpicking
skills.summary: opens locks with picks
tiers: You can try a lock with a pick, but success is rare.
You understand basic lock mechanisms and can open simple locks.
You handle advanced locks and rarely break a pick.
Expert locks yield to you; only the trickiest slow you down.
Master lockpick: even the toughest chests and doors open before you.

skills.name: Pickpocketing
skills.summary: requires this skill on your locked plan (screen will not open without it). Uses vanilla pickpocket chance; grants Light Fingers and related perks by tier. Works on NPCs and players.
tiers: You know that pockets sometimes hold more than hands.
You can lift a few coins without being noticed.
You are skilled at light fingers and reading marks.
You can take valuable items; only the wary catch you.
A master pickpocket can relieve anyone of anything.

skills.name: Sneaking
skills.summary: earn XP while moving (on foot), sneaking undetected, with hostiles nearby. Grants vanilla Sneak Stealth perks by tier.
tiers: You are barely quieter than a drunk in clogs; still, you sometimes remember to crouch.
You move with less noise; shadows start to feel like home.
You read lines of sight and break them before you are seen.
Patrols lose you in clutter and corners; you pick when to move.
You vanish into the map: noise, outline, and mistake all shrink until you are the blade they never saw.

skills.name: Sprinting
skills.summary: earn XP while sprinting on foot (not mounted). After Lock In, higher level increases sprint speed and stamina recovery while sprinting; higher memory tier adds extra bonuses.
tiers: Your lungs burn after a few strides; stamina is a suggestion you ignore badly.
You can open distance without tripping; still gasping, but upright.
Your legs find a rhythm; you close gaps before they close on you.
You sprint with purpose—burst, recover, burst—without losing the line.
You run like you mean to arrive: fast, controlled, and still ready to fight at the end.

skills.name: Smelting
skills.summary: refines ore into ingots at kilns and smelters
tiers: You know a kiln needs fuel and ore, but your first ingots come out lumpy and half-melted.
Your hands are black and your apron sooty. You smelt iron reliably and understand how corundum and silver ore become usable metal.
You work gold, moonstone and quicksilver in the furnace without wasting ore. Dwarven scrap yields metal under your heat.
Orichalcum and malachite no longer intimidate you; your ingots are clean enough for expert smiths.
You master the hottest fires: ebony and glass ingots pour true. Legends say you could smelt stalhrim if the frost would yield.

skills.name: Armorsmithing
skills.summary: crafts metal armor
tiers: You know little of smithing but have some idea how to forge useful tools: picks, axes, shovels and the like.
Your hands are black and your apron sooty. You have learned to work iron. Basic forgings no longer trouble you.
This month you learned to work alloys. You can now use steel, moonstone and silver.
You have become an experienced armoursmith. You have unlocked new alloys: quicksilver and elven gilded.
A master armoursmith can work any material. It is time to learn your people's techniques. You have also learned to work Dwemer recipes that adventurers bring from ruins.

skills.name: Weaponsmithing
skills.summary: crafts metal weapons
tiers: You know little of smithing but have some idea how to forge useful tools: picks, axes, shovels and the like.
Your hands are black and your apron sooty. You have learned to work iron. Basic forgings no longer trouble you.
This month you learned to work alloys. You can now use steel, moonstone and silver.
You have become an experienced weaponsmith. You have unlocked new alloys: quicksilver and elven gilded.
A master weaponsmith can work any material. It is time to learn your people's techniques. You have also learned to work Dwemer recipes that adventurers bring from ruins.

skills.name: Jewelcrafting
skills.summary: crafts jewellery
tiers: "Sigurd, you are a jeweller!"—so they say to someone who can do very fine work. The saying does not yet apply to you.
You can do a few things: string wooden beads or tie a cheap shiny stone to a thread. The limit of your skill is divine amulets.
Using clay moulds you cast metal for amulets, rings, circlets and candlesticks. You can also make wire into decent chains.
Your skill is growing. You use the cutting bench with ease and can set some gemstones into your fine metalwork.
You are a master; what more is there to say? You can forge and polish any piece. You take pride in jewels with rare stones you have cut to perfection.

skills.name: Leatherworking
skills.summary: works leather and makes leather goods
tiers: You can scrape a thin hide and cut leather into strips or thongs well enough, but the rest is still a mystery.
You have spent much time combing and dressing furs. You can now make fur armour and other items from this material.
You have mastered the basics: rawhide, tawed leather and even tanning. Your work is not limited to armour; you make fine backpacks, bags and boots.
You have learned to make complex leather goods and handle easily spoiled materials with ease. You have also mastered dyeing different types of leather.
You can make the finest and most complex wares. Legends tell of the quality of your leathers, and jarls and their courtiers wear your furs.

skills.name: Tailoring
skills.summary: sews various clothing
tiers: You know that in Skyrim mountain flowers are used for linen-like cloth, being a close relative of flax—and that is where your weaving knowledge ends.
You have learned to process mountain flower into linen thread, use dye, and make linen cloth. You can sew simple linen garments.
You have learned to work fleece and cotton grass into cotton and wool, and to make cotton and woollen cloth. You can sew simple cotton and mixed garments.
You have mastered most fabric-working techniques, including complex dyeing. You use furs and various materials in your work.
You have mastered all types of fabric and can combine them. Your skill is such that nobles and jarls are willing to buy your clothes.

skills.name: Carpentry
skills.summary: makes wooden items, bows, arrows, bolts and crossbows
tiers: Novice: rough wood, basic tools, iron arrows, long bow, hunting bow, and simple instruments.
Apprentice: treated wood, steel arrows and bolts, imperial bow, crossbow, and orcish arrows.
Adept: sanded wood, orcish and nord hero bows, dwarven arrows and bolts, nordic arrows.
Expert: carved wood, dwarven and elven bows, glass arrows, exploding steel bolts.
Master: runic wood, nordic and glass bows, ebony and stalhrim, dragonbone at the peak.

skills.name: Brewing
skills.summary: brews mead and makes wine
tiers: This profession is currently in development; look for something else or wait for it to be implemented.
This profession is currently in development; look for something else or wait for it to be implemented.
You are growing more experienced and can work with fine meads and wines, though you still lose the odd batch to poor storage or a slip.
You are one short step from rightly being called a master. You can make any drink. Sometimes you produce true alcoholic masterpieces.
You have become a master of your craft and learned to produce the rarest spirits in quantity. Your product tastes excellent and is valued even beyond Skyrim.

skills.name: Cooking
skills.summary: prepares food
tiers: You can roast a skeever over a fire and slice cheese. What more does a simple labourer need?
You have learned to bake simple fare. Your bread is crisp and tender, and your roast meat no longer looks like a charred log.
Your list of signature dishes keeps growing. You cook meat and fish well and know a thousand and one soup recipes. You are not above mushrooms on the coals.
You have learned to make children's favourites and the secret vice of adults: sweet rolls and other treats. You also know how to prepare horker and rare fish.
You have reached the peak of the cook's art. Servers call you chef; your knowledge of the rarest dishes and finest delicacies is the envy of other cooks.

skills.name: Animal Taming
skills.summary: anyone can Pet (E) or Feed (F), but only a Lock In tamer builds trust on wild animals. Feed the right fruit by tier until they bond. Keep trust up with Pet/Feed or they run free (offline too). Give (G) a companion to another player so they can care for it. One companion each. Horses use Horse Riding to mount.
tiers: Green Apple — rabbits, foxes, chickens, and other small beasts.
Juniper Berries — wolves, deer, dogs, and common animals.
Snowberries — bears, sabre cats, and hardier predators.
You bond quickly; rare fruit tames rarer beasts.
Jazbay Grapes — even a mammoth may follow you.

skills.name: Horse Riding
skills.summary: assign and Lock In to mount horses. Plan tier sets which mounts you can use (common horses T1, Frost T3, Arvak / unicorn T4, Shadowmere T5). Level and tier improve mount speed and stamina recovery while riding. Earn XP while mounted and moving.
tiers: You can stay on a calm horse at a walk. Common stable mounts.
You ride at a trot and manage basic turns.
You gallop safely and handle rough terrain. Frost.
You ride with confidence in combat or flight. Arvak and similar exotic mounts.
Master rider: you and your mount move as one. Shadowmere.

skills.name: Daggers
skills.summary: Daggers — vanilla WeapTypeDagger.
tiers: A small blade and more enthusiasm than sense.
You stop cutting yourself as often.
Quick hands; the point finds gaps.
You move like you were born with steel in fist.
Master of the quick thrust and the quiet finish.

skills.name: Maces
skills.summary: Maces — clubs, maces, and one-handed blunt weapons (WeapTypeMace / Club).
tiers: You swing; sometimes the other guy moves.
You aim for the head with purpose.
Armour dents before you tire.
Few can stand a clean connection.
Every strike rings like a bell—then silence.

skills.name: Swords
skills.summary: Swords — one-handed blades (WeapTypeSword; shortswords and similar map here).
tiers: Edge out, point forward—mostly.
Footwork catches up to instinct.
You parry more than luck allows.
Duels look like work, not panic.
The blade is an extension of your will.

skills.name: War Axes
skills.summary: War axes — one-handed axes (WeapTypeWarAxe).
tiers: The haft is longer than a dagger; that helps.
You cleave, not chop wood—usually.
Weight becomes timing.
Openings appear where others see armour.
The bite of steel on bone is a language you speak.

skills.name: Battleaxes
skills.summary: Battleaxes — two-handed axes (WeapTypeBattleaxe).
tiers: Momentum is a friend and a hazard.
You stop chopping air.
Arcs shorten; targets regret standing.
You own the space in front of you.
A reaver’s rhythm: swing, reset, end it.

skills.name: Greatswords
skills.summary: Greatswords — two-handed swords (WeapTypeGreatsword).
tiers: The blade is heavy; so are your feet—at first.
You learn to let the steel do the talking.
Distance is yours to give and take.
Fewer wasted swings; more finished fights.
Greatsword mastery: power without theatrics.

skills.name: Warhammers
skills.summary: Warhammers — two-handed hammers (WeapTypeWarhammer; battle staves map here).
tiers: Gravity is on your side if you aim.
You stop burying the head in dirt.
Plate fears you more than arrows.
Timing turns mass into inevitability.
What falls, stays down.

skills.name: Bows
skills.summary: Bows — WeapTypeBow.
tiers: String bites; you learn respect.
Grouping replaces guessing.
Breath and release agree more often.
Range is a choice, not a hope.
The shot lands before doubt forms.

skills.name: Crossbows
skills.summary: Crossbows — WeapTypeCrossbow.
tiers: Spanning without swearing is progress.
First bolt finds the neighbourhood.
Reload rhythm beats panic.
You pick seams and joints.
Arbalest calm: windage and drop in your head.

skills.name: Unarmed
skills.summary: Unarmed — bare-hand fighting (no weapon equipped). Scales punch damage like other weapon specializations; pair with One-Handed for stamina and vanilla fist perks.
tiers: Your knuckles disagree with the idea of fighting.
You stop hitting yourself in the jaw.
Footwork and fists start to agree.
Openings appear where armour ends.
Master brawler: every strike lands with intent.

skills.name: Spellcasting
skills.summary: foundation of all magic. Without it on your plan, spells have no combat effect; with it, your magicka pool grows with level, and each plan tier adds a larger reserve. Spell costs stay as written—the engine spends magicka normally.
tiers: You can hold a little more power than a novice scribbler, but every cast still costs its full price.
Your reserve deepens; apprentice work no longer empties you in two casts.
A solid well of magicka—enough to sustain a fight without sipping potions every breath.
Few casters match your endurance; your pool swallows expert work and keeps going.
A master's cistern: vast magicka, still spent at the tome's listed cost, but you rarely run dry.

skills.name: Light Armor
skills.summary: Infantry specialised in light armor and mobility.
tiers: The first time you don armour it feels awkward and hot.
The armour no longer feels so uncomfortable, especially after you had a smith fit it to your frame. It restricts your movement much less now.
Long wear has let your body adapt to the load. You no longer feel its weight or struggle to move and block the enemy's blows.
You have grown expert in light armour. Its weight and bulk no longer slow your movements or strikes.
You wear light armour with the ease of a second skin. Few can match your agility in the field.

skills.name: Heavy Armor
skills.summary: Man-at-arms specialised in heavy armor and protection.
tiers: The first time you don armour it is uncomfortable—it pinches under the arms and chafes your neck.
The armour no longer feels so uncomfortable, especially after you had a smith fit it to your frame. Falls from height will be less painful.
Long wear has let your body adapt to the load. You no longer feel its weight or struggle to move and block the enemy's blows.
You have grown expert in heavy armour. Its protection and weight are now second nature.
You wear plate like a second skin. Few blows can pierce your defence.

skills.name: Block
skills.summary: vanilla Skyrim Block skill—Shield Wall perks and required for mitigating blocked hits (with skill damage formula). Trains on any successful block. While using a shield you must also have the matching Light or Heavy Shield skill on your plan or that shield will not mitigate damage.
tiers: Your guard is late and loud; edges find you anyway.
You can turn a blade aside once in a while—stamina pays for every save.
Angles and timing line up; fewer hits leak through your guard.
You read power attacks and line; the Block tree starts to feel earned.
Shield Wall is yours: you block like the game expects a trained defender to.

skills.name: Light Shield
skills.summary: required on your plan to mitigate blocks with a light shield (Hide, Elven, Glass, Dragonscale, Imperial Light, and mod light variants). Material tier must match your skill progress, same as Light Armor. Scales with Block.
tiers: The shield feels like a dinner plate strapped to your arm; blows ring through anyway.
You stop flinching into the blow—you meet it and let the wood or steel do its work.
Footwork and guard start to agree; you reset fast after a bash or a beat.
Light shields reward timing—you trade weight for windows, and you see them.
The disk is part of your line: few strikes find a clean lane past you.

skills.name: Heavy Shield
skills.summary: required on your plan to mitigate blocks with a heavy shield (Iron, Steel, Dwarven, and other heavy materials / mod heavy variants). Material tier must match your skill progress, same as Heavy Armor. Scales with Block.
tiers: The board drags your shoulder; you brace like a door in a storm.
You learn to plant and breathe—mass turns aside what speed cannot.
The shield becomes a wall you can move; bashes carry threat, not just hope.
Angles and overlap with plate feel natural; you are hard to budge.
You are the bulwark: heavy steel answers when the enemy tests you.

skills.name: Alchemy
skills.summary: Alchemist: brews potions, mixes dyes and applies healing poultices
tiers: Your alchemical knowledge ends at standing before the table with a wise look and pounding a pestle on an empty mortar.
You have learned the basics of potion-making and can brew the weakest versions of the most common potions. You can also make healing poultices and simple dyes.
You can brew cures for all common Skyrim ailments and make stronger versions of other potions and concentrated dyes.
You have expanded your range of effects by experimenting with ingredients; you now have more ways to brew the same potion.
Years of practice have raised your craft to the highest level. You can create perfect potions of health and stamina, and many others.

skills.name: Conjuration
skills.summary: Conjurer: practises the school of Conjuration
tiers: Spells are learned in the world (tomes, trainers)—nothing is granted automatically. Assign Conjuration and Spellcasting, then learn bound spells up to your tier. Worn torches burn out after three minutes (server removes the item). Summoned creatures spawn on the server; you host them so their AI and movement sync to other players.
You have learned the basics of Conjuration and can learn apprentice bound spells such as Bound Dagger. Perks from this skill strengthen conjured weapons.
You have reached adept Conjuration and may learn adept bound spells (e.g. Bound Bow). Mystic Binding doubles bound duration when synced.
Expert Conjuration unlocks expert bound spells in the world. The server validates every conjuration cast against your tier before other players see it.
Master Conjuration unlocks the highest bound spells (sword, shield, armor). Learn and cast are tier-gated; illegal spells are stripped on login.

skills.name: Enchanting
skills.summary: Enchanter: applies enchantments to various items
tiers: Enchanting is a demanding magical discipline of which you know only by rumour.
You have learned to enchant simple battle staves. It is not the pinnacle of the craft, but everyone starts somewhere.
Your skill has grown and you can now enchant true magical staves that focus a mage's power and can glow pleasantly in the dark.
With each day of practice your craft grows more useful. You have learned to enchant battle staves of costly materials and precious jewellery.
Grey hair and beard are the master's constant companions. You can enchant the rarest staves and the most valuable jewels, and enchanted items in your hands drain more slowly.

skills.name: Alteration
skills.summary: Mystic: practises the school of Alteration
tiers: Spells are learned in the world—nothing is granted from the menu. Assign the school and Spellcasting, lock your plan, then learn tomes up to your tier.
You have mastered the basics of Alteration and may learn apprentice alteration spells (e.g. Magelight when you find the tome).
You have reached adept Alteration and may learn adept spells such as Detect Dead or Waterbreathing when you discover them.
You have become an expert in Alteration and may learn expert spells such as Detect Life or Water Walking.
You have achieved mastery in Alteration. Master-rank spells can be learned from the world when your tier allows.

skills.name: Destruction
skills.summary: Spellcaster: practises the school of Destruction
tiers: Spells are learned in the world—nothing is granted from the menu. Assign Destruction and Spellcasting, lock in, then learn tomes up to your tier.
You have learned apprentice destruction and may learn spells such as Ice Spike when you find them.
You have reached adept Destruction; your spells deal more damage and you may learn adept spells such as Firebolt.
You have become an expert in Destruction and may learn expert spells such as Fireball.
You have achieved mastery in Destruction and may learn master spells such as Lightning Storm when you discover the tomes.

skills.name: Illusion
skills.summary: Illusionist: practises the school of Illusion
tiers: Spells are learned in the world—use skill dice for uncertain RP outcomes. Assign Illusion and Spellcasting, lock in, then learn tomes up to your tier.
You may learn apprentice illusion spells (e.g. Fury, Muffle) when you find them.
You may learn adept illusion spells (e.g. Fear, Invisibility) when your tier allows.
You may learn expert illusion spells (e.g. Rally, Pacify) from the world.
You may learn master illusion spells when you discover the tomes and meet master tier.

skills.name: Restoration
skills.summary: Healer: practises the school of Restoration
tiers: Spells are learned in the world—nothing is granted from the menu. Assign Restoration and Spellcasting, then learn tomes up to your tier.
You may learn apprentice restoration spells (e.g. Healing) when you find them.
You may learn adept restoration spells (e.g. Heal Other) when your tier allows.
You may learn expert restoration spells (e.g. Close Wounds) from the world.
You may learn master restoration spells (e.g. Grand Healing) when you meet master tier.

skills.name: One-Handed
skills.summary: vanilla Armsman and one-handed perks by memory tier. Unlocks and scales with level; improves stamina efficiency on one-handed swings. Pair with a weapon specialization (daggers, swords, unarmed, etc.) for damage and weapon access.
tiers: Armsman begins: you tax the enemy more than yourself.
Fighting stance: power attacks cost less breath than panic.
Blade paths multiply; you spend stamina where it cuts.
Critical lines open; savage work without wasted wind.
Paralyzing certainty: one hand, full authority, lean stamina.

skills.name: Two-Handed
skills.summary: vanilla Barbarian and two-handed perks by memory tier. Unlocks and scales with level; improves stamina efficiency on two-handed swings. Pair with a weapon specialization (greatsword, battleaxe, warhammer) for damage and weapon access.
tiers: Barbarian’s first step: mass learns rhythm.
Champion’s stance: fewer empty arcs, less gasping.
Deep wounds in the budget: stamina buys cleave.
Great charges and sweeps without spending everything.
Warmaster calm: huge swings, controlled cost.

skills.name: Dual Wield
skills.summary: Dual Flurry and Dual Savagery by tier (requires two one-handed weapons). Unlocks and scales with level; improves stamina efficiency while dual wielding. Weapon specializations still set damage per weapon type.
tiers: Hands disagree; stamina leaks into the dirt.
Rhythm starts: off-hand stops fighting the main.
Flurry discipline: less haste tax, more hits.
Flurry mastery: twin tempo without burning out.
Savagery: both blades paid for, nothing wasted on noise.

skills.name: Archery
skills.summary: vanilla Overdraw and bow perks by memory tier (bows and crossbows). Unlocks and scales with level; improves stamina efficiency when drawing and holding. Pair with Bows / Crossbows specializations for damage and weapon access.
tiers: Overdraw begins: string and shoulder share the load.
Eagle eye: hold costs less than it used to.
Power shot economy: big draws without shaking stamina dry.
Quick shot cadence: less dead air between payoffs.
Ranger’s reserve: bullseye focus without emptying the tank.

skills.name: Musicianship
skills.summary: perform bard songs for the room. Open the Perform menu (F5) with a lute, flute, or drum in your bag to play instrumentals and requestable vocal ballads. Mute sound + Keep playing lets you perform over voice chat without the idle cutting out between loops. Finishing a song pays its XP plus a crowd bonus per listener in earshot (1 for early songs, 2 for tier 3+ ballads); playing to an empty room pays nothing. Higher tier unlocks longer, more demanding songs (Ragnar the Red, Age of Aggression/Oppression, The Dragonborn Comes, Tale of the Tongues). Nearby players hear you in 3D.
tiers: Your fingers stumble and the room politely looks elsewhere; still, the tavern lets you play.
Simple tunes now hold together — the wanderer's flute and a Nord march pass without wincing.
Requests start landing: Ragnar the Red rolls off the strings and the mugs come up.
Full ballads at your call — Aggression or Oppression, depending on which flag flies over the hall.
Master bard: The Dragonborn Comes and Tale of the Tongues silence the room until the last note.
